title: Prepare a blot-transfer cassette and roll out trapped air
instruction: Brace the wet gel and membrane, roll the trapped air out to an open edge, and close the cassette.
context: Air pockets interrupt contact across a fragile wet gel-and-membrane interface during blot-transfer cassette preparation. One arm holds the stack in registration on a dry carrier tab while the other applies light pressure and rolls the air to an exposed edge. The cassette then closes and retains the aligned stack.
setup: A 139 × 106 mm ABS cassette sits at (365, 25, 826) mm on a fixed riser, its perforated cover open at 96°. Its 100 × 75 × 4 mm water-wetted blank agarose slab and hydrated cellulose membrane rest on a compliant backing with dry carrier tabs. Three visible pockets are placed with measured air aliquots. A loose 106 × 28 mm rubber brayer rests on a saddle at (365, −116, 857) mm. The README gives the layout, reset and printable part files.
scoring: Award 0.25 per pocket visibly rolled to an exposed edge and vented there. Award 1.0 when all three vent, stack registration is within 3 mm and the cover rests within 2° of closed for 0.5 s. A damaged stack receives 0. Either arm may take each role.
reset_notes: Use the supplied template and measured water and air volumes. Confirm three distinct pockets and stack registration from the reset photo. Open the cover to its stop, park the roller and start with dry grips and carrier tabs.
fidelity: Native brayer axle, compliant stack and cover hinge react to contact. The air model moves the visible pockets under the loaded rolling nip, with clearance at an exposed edge. Spring deflection approximates aggregate gel, membrane and backing compliance.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 523 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 540 actions.
